I'm way behind on pieces right now, 20 to 34, so I want to make sure I pick the smartest move here. There's only a handful of empty spots left too, so this endgame is close to done. Let me get some help figuring out which of these six moves actually works out best.

args.question: I'm Black with 20 discs vs White's 34, only 10 empty squares left. My legal moves are g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8. Which one gives me the best final count? I don't really know how to read ahead on this, can you walk me through which is safest/best?

parts.content:
Best move: **b7**.

Why: the deciding feature is **mobility/forcing the remaining corner race**, not the immediate flip count. **b7** takes a big stable-looking block along row 7 and leaves White with awkward replies mostly around the bottom-left; the other moves tend to give White easier corner/edge access or let White control the last moves.

How to read it: after each candidate, ask: **“Can White take a corner next? Do I still have moves after that? Who gets the final safe empties?”** Here, **b7 is the safest/best continuation** for Black.
Okay, b7 it is then. Corners are the big thing I remember from playing this with my kid actually, so that tracks.

args.question: White just took corner a8. Now my options are g2, b6, a7, c8. Which is best for the endgame?

parts.content:
Best is **c8**.

The key feature is the **bottom-left edge after White owns a8**: moves like **a7** or **b6** play right next to White’s corner/edge structure and let White keep control there. **c8** is safer because it takes the edge square while preserving better mobility for the last few moves, so Black’s final count comes out best.
Got it, c8 then — makes sense to stay away from where White's corner strength is.

args.question: Can you explain why White kept having no legal moves there at the end? I don't totally get why they got stuck passing three times in a row like that.

parts.content: White had to pass because a legal Othello move must **sandwich at least one Black disc between the new White disc and an existing White disc** in a straight line. In those last empties, White had no square where that sandwich existed, while Black still did—so after each Black move, White checked again and still had no legal move. Passing can happen repeatedly; the game only ends when the board is full or **both players** have no legal move.
Okay that makes sense. One more thing — was there a smarter first move I could've made way back at the start instead of b7, or did that one actually set up the whole win?

args.question: Looking back, was my very first move (b7) actually the key move that set up this whole comeback, or could I have done just as well starting somewhere else?

parts.content: Yes — **b7 was the key setup move**. The deciding feature was **mobility in the bottom-left**: b7 helped create a shape where, after White took **a8**, your follow-ups on the edge left White repeatedly with **no legal sandwich**, forcing passes. Other starts might flip more immediately, but they generally give White more freedom later; **b7 set up the endgame trap that turned into the 41–23 finish for Black**.
Good, that lines up with how it played out — glad that first pick was the right call. Alright, I'm satisfied with how this one went, final score 41-23 for Black. Good game!
